# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 762
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/762
- **Title**: gh-760 [GOAL] A persisted provider can never brick the CLI — chatgpt-codex boot-switch hole + degrade-never-crash boot
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-760` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +888
- **Deletions**: -58
- **Created**: 2026-09-21T11:41:02Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T22:50:51Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- `buildCliDefaultModel`'s hand-maintained boot switch never learned the catalog's `chatgpt` entry (kind `chatgpt-codex`): `_ => throw ConfigException('unknown provider')` killed the process at boot before any user input.
- Nothing between the shared, externally-written config / per-folder model state and that switch degraded the value — one unrecognised id bricked the binary. Same class: `roles.*` on an unknown provider hit `_fail` at boot; `inspect_image` silently misrouted unknown kinds to `api.openai.com`.

### Fix
- `provider_catalog.dart`: new `resolveCliProviderSpec(kind, {baseUrl})` — catalog-driven lookup by name AND kind, so every catalog entry (present/future) resolves; unknown ids still throw for direct API callers.
- `startup.dart` + `bin/fah.dart`: saved `chatgpt-codex` restores (AC1); an unknown persisted id degrades — loud stderr warning (bad value, file, fallback taken, version-skew hint; config never mutated) + fallback boot (AC2). Folder-state and `roles:` poisoning degrade the same way instead of throwing.
- `model_resolver.dart`: unknown-provider chain entries skip with a named reason, like missing keys. `headless_provider_key.dart`: key names resolve by kind too (`chatgpt-codex` → `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`). `inspect_image.dart`: explicit `chatgpt-codex` named refusal.

### Test Coverage
- New REG-C1 property (`provider_catalog_coverage_test.dart`): every catalog name+kind resolves — fails at PR time on future drift. New real-binary IT (`poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`): poisoned config boots on fallback with warning and completes a headless turn (IT-B2/AC2, AC1, E3).
- Updated: `startup_test.dart` (AC1/AC2 restore+report), `model_resolver_test.dart` (skip+fallback), `inspect_image_test.dart` (refusal).
- Full suite: 7226 passed, 3 failed, 10 skipped — the 3 are pre-existing `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` failures caused by this shell's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` (pass with env scrubbed; diff doesn't touch the queue). The helper scrub also fixed 3 `fa_llm_mock` tests broken by the same ambient env.

### Notes
- E5 (fully-foreign config → setup wizard) out of scope by design; provider identity canonicalization stays with #706.


### Review round 3 (head e43dabe4)
- Name-vs-kind hole closed everywhere: the saved config AND the folder-state restore now put the RESOLVED spec's adapter kind (never the raw saved string) into `providerKind`; REG-C1 extended to the stream boundary (`resolveEffectiveCliArgs` → `providerStreamFunction` for every catalog name+kind).
- Roles degrade is version-skew-only: `UnknownProviderRoleException` is thrown/caught on a TYPED flag (no skip-reason substring matching — a model id containing the marker words cannot misclassify); any other roles `ConfigException` (e.g. known provider, missing key) hard-fails like pre-#760.
- Roles entries resolve adapter kinds too (`chatgpt-codex` is known); headless test children run on a credential-scrubbed env (`FA_*`, `*_API_KEY/_TOKEN/_SECRET/_KEY/_CREDENTIALS`).
- Diff hygiene: all riding format-only churn (14 files), the stale factory-pin flip, and every memory/note change reverted — the diff is exactly gh-760 scope (12 files, +888/−58).
- The `/dap` menu `waitForScreen` flake fix (#550 family, reddened the integ-mock leg on d331157b) moved to its own PR: #776 (`fix/dap-tui-menu-waitfor`).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 762
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/762
- **Title**: gh-760 [GOAL] A persisted provider can never brick the CLI — chatgpt-codex boot-switch hole + degrade-never-crash boot
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-760` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +888
- **Deletions**: -58
- **Created**: 2026-09-21T11:41:02Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T22:50:51Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- `buildCliDefaultModel`'s hand-maintained boot switch never learned the catalog's `chatgpt` entry (kind `chatgpt-codex`): `_ => throw ConfigException('unknown provider')` killed the process at boot before any user input.
- Nothing between the shared, externally-written config / per-folder model state and that switch degraded the value — one unrecognised id bricked the binary. Same class: `roles.*` on an unknown provider hit `_fail` at boot; `inspect_image` silently misrouted unknown kinds to `api.openai.com`.

### Fix
- `provider_catalog.dart`: new `resolveCliProviderSpec(kind, {baseUrl})` — catalog-driven lookup by name AND kind, so every catalog entry (present/future) resolves; unknown ids still throw for direct API callers.
- `startup.dart` + `bin/fah.dart`: saved `chatgpt-codex` restores (AC1); an unknown persisted id degrades — loud stderr warning (bad value, file, fallback taken, version-skew hint; config never mutated) + fallback boot (AC2). Folder-state and `roles:` poisoning degrade the same way instead of throwing.
- `model_resolver.dart`: unknown-provider chain entries skip with a named reason, like missing keys. `headless_provider_key.dart`: key names resolve by kind too (`chatgpt-codex` → `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`). `inspect_image.dart`: explicit `chatgpt-codex` named refusal.

### Test Coverage
- New REG-C1 property (`provider_catalog_coverage_test.dart`): every catalog name+kind resolves — fails at PR time on future drift. New real-binary IT (`poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`): poisoned config boots on fallback with warning and completes a headless turn (IT-B2/AC2, AC1, E3).
- Updated: `startup_test.dart` (AC1/AC2 restore+report), `model_resolver_test.dart` (skip+fallback), `inspect_image_test.dart` (refusal).
- Full suite: 7226 passed, 3 failed, 10 skipped — the 3 are pre-existing `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` failures caused by this shell's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` (pass with env scrubbed; diff doesn't touch the queue). The helper scrub also fixed 3 `fa_llm_mock` tests broken by the same ambient env.

### Notes
- E5 (fully-foreign config → setup wizard) out of scope by design; provider identity canonicalization stays with #706.


### Review round 3 (head e43dabe4)
- Name-vs-kind hole closed everywhere: the saved config AND the folder-state restore now put the RESOLVED spec's adapter kind (never the raw saved string) into `providerKind`; REG-C1 extended to the stream boundary (`resolveEffectiveCliArgs` → `providerStreamFunction` for every catalog name+kind).
- Roles degrade is version-skew-only: `UnknownProviderRoleException` is thrown/caught on a TYPED flag (no skip-reason substring matching — a model id containing the marker words cannot misclassify); any other roles `ConfigException` (e.g. known provider, missing key) hard-fails like pre-#760.
- Roles entries resolve adapter kinds too (`chatgpt-codex` is known); headless test children run on a credential-scrubbed env (`FA_*`, `*_API_KEY/_TOKEN/_SECRET/_KEY/_CREDENTIALS`).
- Diff hygiene: all riding format-only churn (14 files), the stale factory-pin flip, and every memory/note change reverted — the diff is exactly gh-760 scope (12 files, +888/−58).
- The `/dap` menu `waitForScreen` flake fix (#550 family, reddened the integ-mock leg on d331157b) moved to its own PR: #776 (`fix/dap-tui-menu-waitfor`).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a restored `chatgpt-codex` + non-default `baseUrl` now hard-fails headless boot with self-contradictory guidance**

`_keySpec` makes the `chatgpt` spec resolvable for the kind, so `optionalProviderApiKey` now classifies **any** baseUrl other than `chatGptCodexBaseUrl` as a custom endpoint and skips the env-name path — requiring an endpoint-scoped `FA_KEY_<HOST>` store key instead. `_requiredProviderApiKey` then reports `missing API key: set CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS in the environment` **even when that variable is set** (it was just skipped).

Verified against the real binary on this branch (scrubbed `FA_PROVIDER_*`, temp HOME):

```
# ~/.fah/config.yaml
provider: chatgpt-codex
model: gpt-5-codex
baseUrl: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1   # the default every CLI-persisted config carries
# CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS=dummy-creds in env

fa: missing API key: set CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS in the environment   # exit 64
```

The same happens with any custom baseUrl (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:9/v1`). Two consequences:

1. **The realistic partial-write shape refuses to boot headless.** A surface (or a hand-edit fixing the original crash) that writes `provider: chatgpt-codex` over an existing config keeps the stale `baseUrl:` — `CliConfig` persists a baseUrl on every write, and the default is `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`. Pre-PR, this exact config restored the parsed default (`openai-completions` + that baseUrl = the OpenRouter default endpoint) and **booted**; post-PR it exits 64 at the key gate. For headless surfaces (the shared-config family this PR targets) that is still a boot refusal, one step removed from the crash gh-760 set out to kill — the "persisted provider can never brick the CLI" headline doesn't yet cover a persisted provider/baseUrl *pair*.
2. **The error text is wrong** — it names an env var that is set; the actual cause is endpoint-scoped key resolution (`#40` rule) on a mismatched baseUrl. The user cannot fix it by following the message.

Suggested directions (pick one, and pin it in the ITs):

- Treat a restored provider whose saved baseUrl matches *another* catalog default (or any URL that isn't its spec's) as the same version-skew/poison class: warn + fall back, or use the spec's default baseUrl for the restored provider (the pair is internally inconsistent);
- or keep the custom-endpoint key rule but make the required-key error endpoint-aware (`custom endpoint <url>: set FA_KEY_<HOST> via /key set — env names apply only to <spec.defaultBaseUrl>`).

The interactive REPL is unaffected (key optional, OAuth re-establishes on demand), which is why this is IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the chatgpt-codex ITs stop at the key gate, not the provider call — the injected credentials are never used**

The AC1 test (and the `provider: chatgpt` name-form test at line ~237) point `baseUrl:` at the mock server and inject `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS: dummy-creds`. Because the mock URL ≠ `chatGptCodexBaseUrl`, `optionalProviderApiKey` classifies it as a **custom endpoint** and skips the env name — so the boot actually ends at `_requiredProviderApiKey` with `fa: missing API key: set CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS in the environment` (exit 64), *before* any provider call. Verified by running the same shape manually against this branch.

The assertions (`isNot(contains('unknown provider'))`, no `crash.log`) pass for both "reached the provider call" **and** "refused at the key gate", so the test pins less than its comment claims ("the boot MUST reach the provider call instead of dying at model construction") — the `dummy-creds` injection is theater. A regression in the codex provider-call path would not be caught by this test.

Please make the expected outcome explicit, e.g.:

- assert the pinned current contract: `result.stderr` contains `missing API key: set CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` (custom-endpoint codex restore → key-gate exit), and drop the dead `extraEnv`; **or**
- if the intended contract is that the restored codex provider boots headless on env creds, route the test so the creds resolve (config without `baseUrl:`, i.e. the spec default) and assert it gets past the key gate (a distinct codex-wire error from the provider call, still no crash signature).

Related small gap: `headless_provider_key_test.dart` was not extended — there is no unit pin for the `_keySpec` kind resolution this PR adds (`apiKeyEnvNames('chatgpt-codex')` → `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`; `optionalProviderApiKey` env-first / store-fallback / custom-endpoint scoping for the kind). The file already has the copilot pattern to copy. Without it, the fourth production change in this PR ships with no direct test.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.

`_keySpec` makes the `chatgpt` spec resolvable for the kind, so `optionalProviderApiKey` now classifies **any** baseUrl other than `chatGptCodexBaseUrl` as a custom endpoint and skips the env-name path — requiring an endpoint-scoped `FA_KEY_<HOST>` store key instead. `_requiredProviderApiKey` then reports `missing API key: set CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS in the environment` **even when that variable is set** (it was just skipped).

```

provider: chatgpt-codex
model: gpt-5-codex
baseUrl: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1   # the default every CLI-persisted config carries
```

2. **The error text is wrong** — it names an env var that is set; the actual cause is endpoint-scoped key resolution (`#40` rule) on a mismatched baseUrl. The user cannot fix it by following the message.

arguments.content:
💡 **SUGGESTION: the roles degrade drops the whole resolver — including auxiliary roles that may be fine**

On `UnknownProviderRoleException` the boot sets `rolesResolver = null`, which disables not only the poisoned `default` role but also `smol`/`slow`/`plan` chains from the same config that may be perfectly usable — compaction silently falls back to the main model for the whole session with no notice about the aux roles. If the default chain is version-skewed, the skew usually affects all roles, so the blunt form is defensible; but a cheaper variant is to keep the resolver and let `resolveRole(default)`'s failure alone degrade (the aux-role resolutions are already guarded — `task_executor` catches `on Object`, compaction goes through `_maybeAutoCompact`'s best-effort path). If the current behavior is intended, a one-line comment here saying aux roles are deliberately dropped with the default would prevent the next reader from "fixing" it.

💡 **SUGGESTION: kind→spec resolution is first-match and case/trim inconsistent — pin it before it drifts**

Three properties of the new kind lookups that are fine today but order/normalization-dependent:

1. **First-match over a shared kind.** `openai-completions` is the kind of four specs (`openrouter`, `kimi`, `openai`, `codemie`). `resolveCliProviderSpec` special-cases the bare kind so its loop never fires for it, but `_keySpec` (`headless_provider_key.dart`) and `_kindProvider` (`model_resolver.dart`) resolve the shared kind by **insertion order** — currently `openrouter`, which happens to match every legacy expectation (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY` pair). In a `FA_PROVIDERS`-filtered build, `_kindProvider` honors the filter while `_keySpec` doesn't, so the same kind can resolve to *different* specs in the two layers. A future catalog entry inserted ahead of `openrouter` (or a filtered build) silently changes which spec a bare kind means. Consider an explicit canonical-kind→spec mapping, or at least a test pinning the winner for shared kinds.
2. **Normalization mismatch.** `resolveCliProviderSpec` lowercases the name lookup but compares kinds case-sensitively (`spec.kind == key`); `_keySpec`'s kind loop likewise, while its first line (`catalogProvider`) trims+lowercases. So a saved `CHATGPT` resolves (name path) but `CHATGPT-CODEX` degrades with a version-skew warning (kind path). Harmless (warn, don't crash) — but one `toLowerCase()` on the kind comparison would make both paths uniform.
3. `_keySpec`'s doc says "Intentionally NOT honoring the build-time provider filter", but its *first* line (`catalogProvider`) does honor it — only the kind fallback bypasses it. Worth aligning the comment with the code (or the code with the comment) so the stance reads as designed rather than accidental.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 762
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/762
- **Title**: gh-760 [GOAL] A persisted provider can never brick the CLI — chatgpt-codex boot-switch hole + degrade-never-crash boot
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-760` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +888
- **Deletions**: -58
- **Created**: 2026-09-21T11:41:02Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T22:50:51Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- `buildCliDefaultModel`'s hand-maintained boot switch never learned the catalog's `chatgpt` entry (kind `chatgpt-codex`): `_ => throw ConfigException('unknown provider')` killed the process at boot before any user input.
- Nothing between the shared, externally-written config / per-folder model state and that switch degraded the value — one unrecognised id bricked the binary. Same class: `roles.*` on an unknown provider hit `_fail` at boot; `inspect_image` silently misrouted unknown kinds to `api.openai.com`.

### Fix
- `provider_catalog.dart`: new `resolveCliProviderSpec(kind, {baseUrl})` — catalog-driven lookup by name AND kind, so every catalog entry (present/future) resolves; unknown ids still throw for direct API callers.
- `startup.dart` + `bin/fah.dart`: saved `chatgpt-codex` restores (AC1); an unknown persisted id degrades — loud stderr warning (bad value, file, fallback taken, version-skew hint; config never mutated) + fallback boot (AC2). Folder-state and `roles:` poisoning degrade the same way instead of throwing.
- `model_resolver.dart`: unknown-provider chain entries skip with a named reason, like missing keys. `headless_provider_key.dart`: key names resolve by kind too (`chatgpt-codex` → `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`). `inspect_image.dart`: explicit `chatgpt-codex` named refusal.

### Test Coverage
- New REG-C1 property (`provider_catalog_coverage_test.dart`): every catalog name+kind resolves — fails at PR time on future drift. New real-binary IT (`poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`): poisoned config boots on fallback with warning and completes a headless turn (IT-B2/AC2, AC1, E3).
- Updated: `startup_test.dart` (AC1/AC2 restore+report), `model_resolver_test.dart` (skip+fallback), `inspect_image_test.dart` (refusal).
- Full suite: 7226 passed, 3 failed, 10 skipped — the 3 are pre-existing `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` failures caused by this shell's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` (pass with env scrubbed; diff doesn't touch the queue). The helper scrub also fixed 3 `fa_llm_mock` tests broken by the same ambient env.

### Notes
- E5 (fully-foreign config → setup wizard) out of scope by design; provider identity canonicalization stays with #706.


### Review round 3 (head e43dabe4)
- Name-vs-kind hole closed everywhere: the saved config AND the folder-state restore now put the RESOLVED spec's adapter kind (never the raw saved string) into `providerKind`; REG-C1 extended to the stream boundary (`resolveEffectiveCliArgs` → `providerStreamFunction` for every catalog name+kind).
- Roles degrade is version-skew-only: `UnknownProviderRoleException` is thrown/caught on a TYPED flag (no skip-reason substring matching — a model id containing the marker words cannot misclassify); any other roles `ConfigException` (e.g. known provider, missing key) hard-fails like pre-#760.
- Roles entries resolve adapter kinds too (`chatgpt-codex` is known); headless test children run on a credential-scrubbed env (`FA_*`, `*_API_KEY/_TOKEN/_SECRET/_KEY/_CREDENTIALS`).
- Diff hygiene: all riding format-only churn (14 files), the stale factory-pin flip, and every memory/note change reverted — the diff is exactly gh-760 scope (12 files, +888/−58).
- The `/dap` menu `waitForScreen` flake fix (#550 family, reddened the integ-mock leg on d331157b) moved to its own PR: #776 (`fix/dap-tui-menu-waitfor`).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest

Three properties of the new kind lookups that are fine today but order/normalization-dependent:

2. **Normalization mismatch.** `resolveCliProviderSpec` lowercases the name lookup but compares kinds case-sensitively (`spec.kind == key`); `_keySpec`'s kind loop likewise, while its first line (`catalogProvider`) trims+lowercases. Harmless (warn, don't crash) — but one `toLowerCase()` on the kind comparison would make both paths uniform.

💡 **SUGGESTION: an explicitly empty `provider:` now produces the version-skew warning**

`CliConfig` maps a present-but-empty `provider: ""` to the empty string (only an absent key gets the `'openai-completions'` default), and `resolveCliProviderSpec('')` returns null — so a blank value (hand-edit artifact, a surface clearing the field, yaml quirk) now emits the loud `unknown provider "" … written by a newer app/CLI version?` warning and falls back. Pre-#760 this shape silently took the default. Degrade-not-crash is fine, but "written by a newer version?" is a misleading diagnosis for a blank value; a `key.trim().isEmpty → null`-style guard here (or treating blank as unset in `loadCliConfig`) would keep the warning for the real version-skew case only.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `runFaHeadlessRaw` duplicates `runFaHeadless`'s spawn + env-scrub block**

The `Process.run('dart', …)` invocation, the `scrubbedChildEnv()` spread, and the six explicit blank `FA_*` overrides are duplicated verbatim between `runFaHeadless` (fa_cube_headless_helper.dart) and `runFaHeadlessRaw` here — the only real difference is the flag list. When the scrub list next needs a new var (or a new `FA_*` boot input appears), one copy will be updated and the other silently won't, and the two IT families will diverge on what "scrubbed" means. Extract a shared `spawnFa({args, env, extraEnv})` (in the helper, next to `scrubbedChildEnv`) that owns the scrub + blanks, and have both callers pass their flags.

- E5 (fully-foreign config → setup wizard) out of scope by design; provider identity canonicalization stays with #706.


### Review round 3 (head e43dabe4)
- Name-vs-kind hole closed everywhere: the saved config AND the folder-state restore now put the RESOLVED spec's adapter kind (never the raw saved string) into `providerKind`; REG-C1 extended to the stream boundary (`resolveEffectiveCliArgs` → `providerStreamFunction` for every catalog name+kind).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1_codex_custom_baseurl_key_gate.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a restored `chatgpt-codex` + non-default `baseUrl` now hard-fails headless boot with self-contradictory guidance**

`_keySpec` makes the `chatgpt` spec resolvable for the kind, so `optionalProviderApiKey` now classifies **any** baseUrl other than `chatGptCodexBaseUrl` as a custom endpoint and skips the env-name path — requiring an endpoint-scoped `FA_KEY_<HOST>` store key instead. `_requiredProviderApiKey` then reports `missing API key: set CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS in the environment` **even when that variable is set** (it was just skipped).

Verified against the real binary on this branch (scrubbed `FA_PROVIDER_*`, temp HOME):

```
# ~/.fah/config.yaml
provider: chatgpt-codex
model: gpt-5-codex
baseUrl: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1   # the default every CLI-persisted config carries
# CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS=dummy-creds in env

fa: missing API key: set CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS in the environment   # exit 64
```

The same happens with any custom baseUrl (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:9/v1`). Two consequences:

1. **The realistic partial-write shape refuses to boot headless.** A surface (or a hand-edit fixing the original crash) that writes `provider: chatgpt-codex` over an existing config keeps the stale `baseUrl:` — `CliConfig` persists a baseUrl on every write, and the default is `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`. Pre-PR, this exact config restored the parsed default (`openai-completions` + that baseUrl = the OpenRouter default endpoint) and **booted**; post-PR it exits 64 at the key gate. For headless surfaces (the shared-config family this PR targets) that is still a boot refusal, one step removed from the crash gh-760 set out to kill — the "persisted provider can never brick the CLI" headline doesn't yet cover a persisted provider/baseUrl *pair*.
2. **The error text is wrong** — it names an env var that is set; the actual cause is endpoint-scoped key resolution (`#40` rule) on a mismatched baseUrl. The user cannot fix it by following the message.

Suggested directions (pick one, and pin it in the ITs):

- Treat a restored provider whose saved baseUrl matches *another* catalog default (or any URL that isn't its spec's) as the same version-skew/poison class: warn + fall back, or use the spec's default baseUrl for the restored provider (the pair is internally inconsistent);
- or keep the custom-endpoint key rule but make the required-key error endpoint-aware (`custom endpoint <url>: set FA_KEY_<HOST> via /key set — env names apply only to <spec.defaultBaseUrl>`).

The interactive REPL is unaffected (key optional, OAuth re-establishes on demand), which is why this is IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING.
"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: kind→spec resolution is first-match and case/trim inconsistent — pin it before it drifts**

Three properties of the new kind lookups that are fine today but order/normalization-dependent:

1. **First-match over a shared kind.** `openai-completions` is the kind of four specs (`openrouter`, `kimi`, `openai`, `codemie`). `resolveCliProviderSpec` special-cases the bare kind so its loop never fires for it, but `_keySpec` (`headless_provider_key.dart`) and `_kindProvider` (`model_resolver.dart`) resolve the shared kind by **insertion order** — currently `openrouter`, which happens to match every legacy expectation (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY` pair). In a `FA_PROVIDERS`-filtered build, `_kindProvider` honors the filter while `_keySpec` doesn't, so the same kind can resolve to *different* specs in the two layers. A future catalog entry inserted ahead of `openrouter` (or a filtered build) silently changes which spec a bare kind means. Consider an explicit canonical-kind→spec mapping, or at least a test pinning the winner for shared kinds.
2. **Normalization mismatch.** `resolveCliProviderSpec` lowercases the name lookup but compares kinds case-sensitively (`spec.kind == key`); `_keySpec`'s kind loop likewise, while its first line (`catalogProvider`) trims+lowercases. So a saved `CHATGPT` resolves (name path) but `CHATGPT-CODEX` degrades with a version-skew warning (kind path). Harmless (warn, don't crash) — but one `toLowerCase()` on the kind comparison would make both paths uniform.
3. `_keySpec`'s doc says "Intentionally NOT honoring the build-time provider filter", but its *first* line (`catalogProvider`) does honor it — only the kind fallback bypasses it. Worth aligning the comment with the code (or the code with the comment) so the stance reads as designed rather than accidental.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 762
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/762
- **Title**: gh-760 [GOAL] A persisted provider can never brick the CLI — chatgpt-codex boot-switch hole + degrade-never-crash boot
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-760` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +888
- **Deletions**: -58
- **Created**: 2026-09-21T11:41:02Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T22:50:51Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- `buildCliDefaultModel`'s hand-maintained boot switch never learned the catalog's `chatgpt` entry (kind `chatgpt-codex`): `_ => throw ConfigException('unknown provider')` killed the process at boot before any user input.
- Nothing between the shared, externally-written config / per-folder model state and that switch degraded the value — one unrecognised id bricked the binary. Same class: `roles.*` on an unknown provider hit `_fail` at boot; `inspect_image` silently misrouted unknown kinds to `api.openai.com`.

### Fix
- `provider_catalog.dart`: new `resolveCliProviderSpec(kind, {baseUrl})` — catalog-driven lookup by name AND kind, so every catalog entry (present/future) resolves; unknown ids still throw for direct API callers.
- `startup.dart` + `bin/fah.dart`: saved `chatgpt-codex` restores (AC1); an unknown persisted id degrades — loud stderr warning (bad value, file, fallback taken, version-skew hint; config never mutated) + fallback boot (AC2). Folder-state and `roles:` poisoning degrade the same way instead of throwing.
- `model_resolver.dart`: unknown-provider chain entries skip with a named reason, like missing keys. `headless_provider_key.dart`: key names resolve by kind too (`chatgpt-codex` → `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`). `inspect_image.dart`: explicit `chatgpt-codex` named refusal.

### Test Coverage
- New REG-C1 property (`provider_catalog_coverage_test.dart`): every catalog name+kind resolves — fails at PR time on future drift. New real-binary IT (`poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`): poisoned config boots on fallback with warning and completes a headless turn (IT-B2/AC2, AC1, E3).
- Updated: `startup_test.dart` (AC1/AC2 restore+report), `model_resolver_test.dart` (skip+fallback), `inspect_image_test.dart` (refusal).
- Full suite: 7226 passed, 3 failed, 10 skipped — the 3 are pre-existing `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` failures caused by this shell's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` (pass with env scrubbed; diff doesn't touch the queue). The helper scrub also fixed 3 `fa_llm_mock` tests broken by the same ambient env.

### Notes
- E5 (fully-foreign config → setup wizard) out of scope by design; provider identity canonicalization stays with #706.


### Review round 3 (head e43dabe4)
- Name-vs-kind hole closed everywhere: the saved config AND the folder-state restore now put the RESOLVED spec's adapter kind (never the raw saved string) into `providerKind`; REG-C1 extended to the stream boundary (`resolveEffectiveCliArgs` → `providerStreamFunction` for every catalog name+kind).
- Roles degrade is version-skew-only: `UnknownProviderRoleException` is thrown/caught on a TYPED flag (no skip-reason substring matching — a model id containing the marker words cannot misclassify); any other roles `ConfigException` (e.g. known provider, missing key) hard-fails like pre-#760.
- Roles entries resolve adapter kinds too (`chatgpt-codex` is known); headless test children run on a credential-scrubbed env (`FA_*`, `*_API_KEY/_TOKEN/_SECRET/_KEY/_CREDENTIALS`).
- Diff hygiene: all riding format-only churn (14 files), the stale factory-pin flip, and every memory/note change reverted — the diff is exactly gh-760 scope (12 files, +888/−58).
- The `/dap` menu `waitForScreen` flake fix (#550 family, reddened the integ-mock leg on d331157b) moved to its own PR: #776 (`fix/dap-tui-menu-waitfor`).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the

`_keySpec` makes the `chatgpt` spec resolvable for the kind, so `optionalProviderApiKey` now classifies **any** baseUrl other than `chatGptCodexBaseUrl` as a custom endpoint and skips the env-name path — requiring an endpoint-scoped `FA_KEY_<HOST>` store key instead. `_requiredProviderApiKey` then reports `missing API key: set CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS in the environment` **even when that variable is set** (it was just skipped).

Verified against the real binary on this branch (scrubbed `FA_PROVIDER_*`, temp HOME):

```
# ~/.fah/config.yaml
provider: chatgpt-codex
model: gpt-5-codex
baseUrl: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1   # the default every CLI-persisted config carries
# CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS=dummy-creds in env

fa: missing API key: set CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS in the environment   # exit 64
```

The same happens with any custom baseUrl (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:9/v1`). Two consequences:

1. **The realistic partial-write shape refuses to boot headless.** A surface (or a hand-edit fixing the original crash) that writes `provider: chatgpt-codex` over an existing config keeps the stale `baseUrl:` — `CliConfig` persists a baseUrl on every write, and the default is `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`. Pre-PR, this exact config restored the parsed default (`openai-completions` + that baseUrl = the OpenRouter default endpoint) and **booted**; post-PR it exits 64 at the key gate. For headless surfaces (the shared-config family this PR targets) that is still a boot refusal, one step removed from the crash gh-760 set out to kill — the "persisted provider can never brick the CLI" headline doesn't yet cover a persisted provider/baseUrl *pair*.
2. **The error text is wrong** — it names an env var that is set; the actual cause is endpoint-scoped key resolution (`#40` rule) on a mismatched baseUrl. The user cannot fix it by following the message.

Suggested directions (pick one, and pin it in the ITs):

- Treat a restored provider whose saved baseUrl matches *another* catalog default (or any URL that isn't its spec's) as the same version-skew/poison class: warn + fall back, or use the spec's default baseUrl for the restored provider (the pair is internally inconsistent);
- or keep the custom-endpoint key rule but make the required-key error endpoint-aware (`custom endpoint <url>: set FA_KEY_<HOST> via /key set — env names apply only to <spec.defaultBaseUrl>`).

The interactive REPL is unaffected (key optional, OAuth re-establishes on demand), which is why this is IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING.

A future catalog entry inserted ahead of `openrouter` (or a filtered build) silently changes which spec a bare kind means. 2. **Normalization mismatch.** `resolveCliProviderSpec` lowercases the name lookup but compares kinds case-sensitively (`spec.kind == key`); `_keySpec`'s kind loop likewise, while its first line (`catalogProvider`) trims+lowercases. Harmless (warn, don't crash) — but one `toLowerCase()` on the kind comparison would make both paths uniform.
3. `_keySpec`'s doc says "Intentionally NOT honoring the build-time provider filter", but its *first* line (`catalogProvider`) does honor it — only the kind fallback bypasses it. ## PR Description

### Root Cause
- `buildCliDefaultModel`'s hand-maintained boot switch never learned the catalog's `chatgpt` entry (kind `chatgpt-codex`): `_ => throw ConfigException('unknown provider')` killed the process at boot before any user input.

### Fix
- `provider_catalog.dart`: new `resolveCliProviderSpec(kind, {baseUrl})` — catalog-driven lookup by name AND kind, so every catalog entry (present/future) resolves; unknown ids still throw for direct API callers.
- `startup.dart` + `bin/fah.dart`: saved `chatgpt-codex` restores (AC1); an unknown persisted id degrades — loud stderr warning (bad value, file, fallback taken, version-skew hint; config never mutated) + fallback boot (AC2).
